claim: The ordinary parser pushes a fresh object on an opening brace, transfers a pending key into the parser stack only when a colon is seen, requires that key to be a string, and transfers the key and pending value into the object on comma or closing brace.
author: codex

claim: Object punctuation distinguishes a missing pending value before comma, a key without a colon, a non-string key at colon, a missing separator between pending values, a trailing comma after a nonempty object, and unmatched closing delimiters.
author: codex

claim: Parser reset releases the pending value and every occupied stack entry, including object containers and pending object keys, while parser free additionally releases reusable stack storage.
author: codex

claim: A duplicate object key replaces the prior slot value without allocating a new slot, so subsequent native iteration retains the original key position while observing the last value.
author: codex

claim: The ordinary parser checks its 10,000-entry limit only before processing a reachable array or object opener, and does so before the pending-value separator check. A validated object colon pushes its pending string key without a depth check, so it may move stackpos from 10,000 to 10,001; comma or close later releases that key entry. Thus 10,000 nested arrays and 5,000 nested keyed objects succeed, their next nested opener rejects, and 9,999 arrays around a final keyed object with a scalar succeed despite the temporary colon overshoot.
author: codex

claim: Pinned parser fixtures exercise empty objects and nested arrays/objects as ordinary JSON values, including objects nested beneath arrays and objects whose values contain arrays.
